title: SSH binary packet protocol
summary: An SSH (RFC 4253) binary packet: 4-byte packet length (big-endian, not including the length field itself or MAC), 1 byte padding length, payload (max 32768 bytes, typically 35000 with extensions), random padding (4-255 bytes, total packet length multiple of cipher block size or 8), then an optional MAC (if not using AEAD).

ext.summary: An SSH (RFC 4253) binary packet: 4-byte packet length (big-endian, not including the length field itself or MAC), 1 byte padding length, payload (max 32768 bytes, typically 35000 with extensions), random padding (4-255 bytes, total packet length multiple of cipher block size or 8), then an optional MAC (if not using AEAD).

structure.meaning: Length of (padding length + payload + padding) in bytes, big-endian. Does not include itself or the MAC.
Number of padding bytes (4-255, or 0 with AEAD ciphers).
The SSH message (key exchange, service request, user auth, channel data, ...).
Random bytes to fill to a block boundary; also hides message length.
Message authentication code (HMAC-SHA1/SHA2) over sequence number + unencrypted packet; omitted with AEAD (chacha20-poly1305, aes-gcm).

notes: Max packet size is 35000 bytes by default (RFC 4253 §6.1), 32768 for the payload.
Padding makes the total (length field excluded) a multiple of the cipher block size (8 for 3DES/Blowfish, 16 for AES).
Each packet has an implicit 32-bit sequence number (per direction) used in the MAC and not transmitted.
AEAD ciphers (chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com, aes128-gcm@openssh.com) fold the MAC into the ciphertext and set padding length to 0.
Compression (zlib@openssh.com) is applied to the payload before encryption if negotiated.
